mappings.note: Mean, mode and median of the mileage table are each computed from the data in separate sub-parts, then compared to pick the safest claim. All three LOs are exercised independently, so no single one can stand for the item.

Median class after an inclusive-to-exclusive conversion, the preceding cumulative frequency and the median itself (LO-3); the mean is then obtained only from 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean, so C-8.1 and not LO-1, which would imply a direct/assumed-mean computation that never happens.
Sub-parts (i) and (ii) recover x and y from the given median (LO-3); (iii) then asks for the upper limit of the modal class (LO-2). The mean is never touched.

Differences a less-than table and finds the median (LO-3), then the modal class and mode (LO-2), then the mean only through the empirical relation (C-8.1). LO-1 is excluded because no mean is computed from the table.

Modal class and mode by formula (LO-2), median estimated from 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean (C-8.1), then the median class located from that value (LO-3). The mean is given, not computed, so LO-1 does not apply.
Median class and median (LO-3), modal class and mode (LO-2), and the mean back-solved from the empirical relation (C-8.1). Median work leads because it occupies the first two sub-parts.

The only genuinely graphical item in the chapter: identifies which plotted curve is the less-than and which the more-than ogive and reads the median off their intersection (C-8.2-LO-1), then gets the mode from the empirical relation (C-8.1). LO-3 is wrong here because no cumulative frequency table is built.
Recovers x from the total, then the median class and median (LO-3) and the modal class and mode (LO-2). The mean is never asked for, unlike the sibling milk-expenditure case studies.

Estimated mean by class marks (LO-1), median interval from cumulative frequencies (LO-3), modal interval and mode by formula (LO-2). The closing empirical-relation step has no LO of its own, but citing all three LOs already covers their shared parent C-8.1.

x from the total and the mean by class marks (LO-1), median class from cumulative frequencies (LO-3), mode by the modal-class formula (LO-2). The final median comes from the empirical relation, which the three LOs' shared parent covers.
